summary: Prefabricated steel lookout on Greenstone Ridge, built 1961, NRHP-listed 2021; standing, no longer staffed, visitors cannot climb it.

facts.design: Prefabricated angle-steel frame on four concrete piers, with a steel-paneled cab
facts.agency: National Park Service (Isle Royale National Park)

access.note: On the Greenstone Ridge Trail in Isle Royale National Park. The NPS says visitors cannot climb the tower.

visit.trail_note: Sits at the junction of the Greenstone Ridge Trail and the Ishpeming Trail. The NPS describes it as a spot for a hiking break.

events.note: Greenstone Ridge Fire swept through part of Isle Royale soon after it became a national park. The NPS memoir says the fire burned over Ishpeming Point.
Construction on this tower began in 1961 per Wikipedia. The NPS memoir says it was constructed that year.
Russell Tabbert, an Isle Royale park ranger, was a lookout here in 1965 (memoir).
Russell Tabbert was a lookout here in 1966 (memoir).
The park changed its fire management strategy by 1968. Wikipedia says the tower was eventually abandoned after that, with no year given.
Russell Tabbert was a lookout here in 1971 (memoir). The source does not say whether the tower was staffed in later years.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places on January 5, 2021.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says the tower was eventually abandoned after the park changed fire strategy by 1968, with no year given. The memoir shows lookouts in the tower in 1971. The story gives no single abandonment year.

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination (Harvey, 2020) is cited on Wikipedia but was not read: the npgallery text URL returned an image, not text. The brief's status and access were 'unknown'; the NPS pages support standing and no climbing. The 1971 event is marked staffed only for the memoir's season; the memoir does not say the tower was staffed later. Wikipedia's tower-height and cab-height figures (about ten feet vs 14 feet) were not used.
